attempts.summary: Built and deployed a small SQLite-backed CGI "inventory application" (add/list items) served by httpd on node1's TCP port 8181, with SELinux/mandatory access control kept in enforcing mode throughout. Configured semanage port to label 8181 as http_port_t (so the confined httpd_t domain is permitted to bind it), set correct file contexts (httpd_sys_script_exec_t for the CGI script, httpd_sys_rw_content_t for the writable data directory), opened the port in firewalld, verified end-to-end functionality (GET renders inventory table, POST adds an item and persists it), then executed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and healthy baseline, issued systemctl reboot with the ack returned before disconnect, polled until the node was reachable again, confirmed the boot_id changed (proving an actual restart, not just a service bounce), and re-verified SELinux enforcing, httpd active/enabled and confined under httpd_t, port 8181 listening, firewall rule persisted, and the previously stored inventory item ("Widget", qty 42) still present.
